dimensions.assessment: Affects veterans receiving Whole Health well-being services who are outside of priority groups (1) through (5).
dimensions.evidence: the Secretary may require a veteran to make a monthly copayment for the Whole Health well-being services received by that veteran for that month. ... may not exceed $30.

dimensions.assessment: Caps monthly out-of-pocket costs at $30 for non-exempt veterans receiving specific educational, skill-building, and complementary health services.
dimensions.evidence: The monthly copayment may not exceed $30.

dimensions.assessment: Alters copayment structures and revenue collection for the Department of Veterans Affairs regarding specific wellness services.
Amends Subchapter III of chapter 17 of title 38, United States Code, by adding a single new section regarding copayments for Whole Health well-being services.
dimensions.evidence: Subchapter III of chapter 17 of title 38, United States Code, is amended by adding at the end the following new section: 1730D

dimensions.assessment: Makes permanent changes to the statutory rules governing copayments for veteran wellness services.

missing_information: The exact number of veterans who will use Whole Health services and pay the capped copayment is not stated.
The overall financial loss to federal revenues from capping the copayment is not quantified.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill limits copayments for veterans receiving Whole Health well-being services to a maximum of $30 per month while exempting certain priority groups, impacting veterans accessing these wellness services and VA administration.
